## 2026-08-08T23:25:42Z run lesson (operator e33)
L019 added (repo): A CI WORKFLOW THAT HAS NEVER RUN IS NOT A GATE, AND 'the local gate passed' IS NOT 'CI passed'. r-001's T004 added .github/workflows/ci.yml and its acceptance criterion was that the CONFIGURATION is valid with Linux/macOS jobs — not that it ever executed. Nothing was pushed for the whole run, so the workflow first ran on 2026-08-06 when the branch was finally pushed for PR #11, and it FAILED on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest, on all three runs that exist. Meanwhile the operator's run-level acceptance was recorded as PASS on the strength of a local 'scripts/ci-local.sh' run. Both statements were true and they were about different things. TWO ROOT CAUSES, both worth generalizing. (1) THE SUITE IS NOT HERMETIC: tests/test_plugins_test.sh asserts binaries_present for codex, claude and agy, which are installed on the author's machine and absent on a runner — so the local gate passes for an environmental reason the CI cannot reproduce. Any suite that can pass because of what happens to be installed is measuring the machine, not the code; PATH-restrict a run and see what actually survives. (2) A CORRECT FIX THAT WAS NEVER GENERALIZED: 'stat -f %m || stat -c %Y' selects the platform on exit status, but GNU stat -f is filesystem mode and can succeed with non-numeric output, so the fallback never fires and the following arithmetic dies under set -u ('File: unbound variable'). T005's implementer diagnosed precisely this and fixed it correctly at libexec/orchid-start:162-165, with the rationale in a comment — and five other sites still carry the raw form, including lib/common.sh:465 which every durable verb's lock acquisition runs through. Same shape as L016: the mechanism existed and nothing made it apply beyond the file that found it. RULE: when a task fixes a portability or safety idiom, grep the tree for the same idiom in the same commit, or file the sweep as its own task — do not leave the fix stranded in the file that discovered it.

## 2026-08-10T00:16:04Z run lesson (operator e33)
L020 added (repo): THE ENGINE-ADAPTER STREAMING LIVENESS ASSERTION IS TIMING-SENSITIVE AND FLAKES, and it has now cost time in two consecutive runs. tests/test_engine_claude.sh and tests/test_engine_agy.sh both assert 'job log must have grown WHILE the adapter was still running (was 0 bytes at the midpoint)' — a stall-detector signal that depends on the stub producing output before an arbitrary midpoint sample. r-001's dogfood notes recorded it flaking once and passing 3/3 isolated; r-002 hit it twice inside a single T013 verification, once in the outer suite and once in the nested vendor-CLI-free suite that tests/test_hermetic_suite.sh runs, where everything is slower and the race widens. Measured: the same assertions pass 3/3 in isolation and the hermetic harness passed cleanly on a re-run with no code change. CONSEQUENCE, which is the expensive part: a flaky assertion inside a whole-suite gate makes VERIFICATION itself unreliable, so a good candidate is sent to rework and burns an attempt for nothing — T013 and T014 between them lost several attempts to this and to the pin hand-off. TREAT A LONE STREAMING/LIVENESS FAILURE AS SUSPECT: re-run the file in isolation before routing a rework, and never let it consume an attempt without that check. The durable fix is to make the assertion wait for a deterministic signal rather than sampling at a midpoint, and it belongs in the same family as the r-001 pipefail flake (L005) — a test whose result depends on scheduling rather than on the code under test.

## 2026-08-10T01:01:03Z T013 intervention (operator e33)
T013 blocked on 'wallclock budget exceeded' — a FALSE POSITIVE, and the cause is a defect r-001 found and r-002 failed to schedule. libexec/orchid-task stamps started_at ONLY when empty, so wallclock_budget_s (28800s) is anchored at the task's FIRST dispatch and measures calendar time ever since, including every hour of operator downtime and debugging. T013 was dispatched around 12:52 and blocked after midnight, so the budget expired on wall time while its actual job work was a fraction of that. PROTOCOL.md describes started_at as stamped by 'task advance ... implementing', which reads as per-advance and does not match the once-only kernel behaviour. r-001 recorded this as a ledger candidate; the operator did not carry it into r-002's requirements, which is why it has now cost a second run a spurious block. Re-anchored to now rather than blocking a candidate whose verification passed clean.

## 2026-08-10T01:58:15Z run lesson (operator e33)
L021 added (repo): REVIEWERS CANNOT TELL AN OPERATOR HAND-OFF FROM AN IMPLEMENTER VIOLATION, and will file the correct action as a defect. On r-002 T013 a reviewer returned a HIGH finding — 'Formula/orchid.rb re-pinned despite the mandatory operator hand-off, with a checksum this session could not have computed' — which is accurate on its facts and wrong in its conclusion: the implementer indeed could not have computed that checksum, because the OPERATOR computed it, which is exactly what the task's own mandatory hand-off clause instructs. The candidate carries operator commits (the formula re-pin, exec bits) interleaved with implementer commits, the review pack shows only a diff, and nothing marks which is which. Consequences: a spurious high finding drives a review-conflict boundary, costs an arbitration, and — worse — teaches whoever reads the record that the hand-off rule was broken when it was followed. This compounds the L017 hand-off design: the more work correctly moves to the operator, the more of the candidate looks like a violation. FIX DIRECTION: mark hand-off commits so they are identifiable (a trailer, a convention, or a field the pack builder reads) and state in the review pack which commits were operator-performed and why, so a reviewer can judge the implementer's work rather than the operator's. Until then, an arbiter must check WHO made a flagged commit before treating it as a defect.

## 2026-08-10T02:57:40Z run lesson (operator e33)
L022 added (repo): PER-CANDIDATE FORMULA PINNING DEADLOCKS EVERY MERGE AFTER THE FIRST. Formula/orchid.rb carries a single content-derived checksum line, and T004's freshness gate made that pin part of EVERY task's verification chain — so every candidate rewrites the same line to a different value. The first task merges fine; the second and every one after it hits 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in Formula/orchid.rb' during merge's stale-base rebase. libexec/orchid-merge:164 aborts the rebase and advances the task to rework, rework dispatches the implementer, and the implementer provably CANNOT resolve it: under the restricted profile (L017) it cannot run git, cannot run scripts/pin-formula.sh, and cannot compute a SHA-256. It therefore produces no commit, the candidate is unchanged, merge is retried, and the same conflict recurs forever. On r-002 this cost T013 a full cycle once T014 became the first merge, and it would have deadlocked all 27 remaining tasks identically. THE DEFECT IS THE DESIGN, NOT THE CONFLICT: a derived artifact must not be pinned per candidate. The pin belongs on the integration branch, regenerated after each merge (or at release), so no task branch ever touches the file and there is nothing to conflict. WORKAROUND UNTIL FIXED: rebase the task branch onto the integration head BEFORE re-pinning, dropping any existing pin commit, so the pin commit never participates in a rebase.

L024 added (repo): THE SUITE IS NOT ISOLATED FROM A CONCURRENTLY RUNNING ORCHID, SO VERIFICATION IS FLAKY BY DESIGN. On r-002, candidate 4bb8d03 of T013 was verified three times with no change to the tree: PASS at 03:44, FAIL at 04:45, PASS again at 05:20 when re-run by hand with nothing else touching the repository. The distinguishing factor is that the two drive-run verifications ran while the drive loop kept polling the repository every 20 seconds, because the driver dispatches verification as a job and continues its passes; the clean re-run had no concurrent orchid. tests/test_notify_channel.sh reaches the operator's REAL $HOME for plugin trust state, so ambient mutation by another orchid process can change what it observes. CONSEQUENCES: a green suite means 'green while the machine was quiet', which is not what CI or a beta qualification claims; and because a spurious failure charges an attempt, flakiness alone walked T013 to 'attempts exhausted' — a block with no supported recovery. This is a hermeticity defect of the same family as the vendor-CLI one, and the hermetic proof does not currently cover it: it removes binaries from PATH but says nothing about ambient state or concurrent writers.

## 2026-08-10T05:52:47Z run lesson (operator e33)
L025 added (repo): VERIFY EVIDENCE CAN BE BOUND TO A COMMIT THAT WAS NEVER THE ONE VERIFIED, WHICH DEFEATS INV-11 FROM THE INSIDE. runners/orchid-drive:634 captures candidate_sha by reading the task worktree's HEAD at the moment it reconciles the implementer envelope, and libexec/orchid-verify then runs the verification command in that same LIVE worktree — at whatever HEAD it holds when the command actually runs, which is not necessarily the captured one. On r-002 T013 the two diverged by 19 minutes: drive advanced implementing -> testing at 05:04:31Z with candidate_sha 4bb8d03, the implementer job kept running and committed 680cfc0 at 05:23:10Z, and the verification that finished at 05:50:15Z therefore exercised 680cfc0 while its evidence header recorded 'sha: 4bb8d03'. Because INV-11's gate on advance testing -> reviewing compares the evidence's recorded sha against the task's CURRENT candidate_sha, and both were 4bb8d03, a PASSING run would have sailed through the gate and certified one commit on the strength of executing a different one. It failed here only by luck — the extra commit made Formula/orchid.rb stale. TWO DEFECTS, both needed: the envelope is treated as a completion signal while the job is still alive and still committing, and verification trusts the worktree instead of the candidate it claims to be verifying. Verification must refuse to run when HEAD does not equal the recorded candidate_sha.

## 2026-08-10T15:27:35Z run lesson (operator e33)
L026 added (repo): A JUDGMENT BOUNDARY ON ONE TASK MUST NOT HALT THE WHOLE RUN. runners/orchid-drive exits 16 as soon as ANY task needs an operator, and the natural reading of that exit — the one this operator's pump implemented, and the one PROTOCOL.md's unattended story invites — is 'stop and fetch a human'. On r-002 that cost seven hours: the pump stopped at T013's review conflict at 07:32Z, the operator arbitrated it within minutes but did not restart the pump, and twenty-eight tasks that had nothing to do with T013 sat idle until 14:42Z. The boundary belonged to ONE task; every other task was dispatchable the entire time. Exit 16 means 'a decision is outstanding somewhere', not 'nothing further can be done', and drive is idempotent, so a boundaried task simply re-reports each pass at no cost. An unattended pump must therefore report the boundary through the notify channel and CONTINUE, halting only when it can make no progress at all. This is not a driver defect — drive did the right thing and reported honestly — it is a defect in what the pump concludes from the report, and it goes directly to the run's claim that unattended operation is real: a pump that stops on the first arbitrable disagreement is attended operation wearing an unattended label.

BOUNDARY EXPLAINED, NOT AN ORCHID DEFECT — OPERATOR ERROR. 'testing -> rework refused (exit 3)' at 21:10:00Z is the tail of a duplicate drive loop the operator left running. While swapping the supervising loop at 20:09Z, 'pgrep -f <script> | head -1' matched only the parent process and the child survived the kill, so TWO loops drove this repository concurrently for about four minutes. Both dispatched a verification for T019. The first finished at 20:36:30Z and correctly advanced testing -> rework on a genuine verify failure. The second finished at 21:10:00Z and tried to make the same transition from a task that was already in rework, which is illegal, so the kernel refused it with exit 3 and raised an operator-decision boundary instead of forcing it. THE KERNEL BEHAVED EXACTLY RIGHT: the transition guard caught a stale actor operating on a task that had moved underneath it, refused to corrupt the state machine, and said so. This is the same hazard class as lesson L024 (the suite is not isolated from a concurrently running orchid) seen from the driver's side rather than the test suite's, and it is worth keeping as positive evidence that the guard works. Operator rule reinforced: never kill a supervising loop by matching one pid; kill the whole match set and verify none survive before starting a replacement. T019 remains correctly in rework at attempts 2 with a real verify failure to brief.

## 2026-08-10T21:21:43Z T023 arbitration (operator e33)
ARBITRATION: REQUEST-CHANGES. The medium is real and the operator confirmed the mechanism in the code. lib/common.sh:518 _worktree_prepare_run ends in 'bash -c "$cmd"' with NO stdin redirection, so the operator's prepare command inherits whatever stdin the driver holds. runners/orchid-drive walks its work with herestring-fed loops — 'while IFS= read -r line; do ... done <<< "$bindings"' at 448/459, and the same shape at 850/867 and 993/1011 — so a prepare command that reads stdin at all (a prompting bootstrap, an installer asking to continue, anything calling read) consumes the REMAINING LINES OF THE LIST THE DRIVER IS ITERATING. The loop then ends early having silently skipped work, with no error anywhere: the driver believes it finished the walk. It generalises past this task: libexec/orchid-verify:40 has the identical '( cd "$cwd" && bash -c "$cmd" )' shape, and the comment in _worktree_prepare_run explicitly claims it runs 'exactly as orchid verify runs its own' — so both want '</dev/null'. The three lows are accepted too, and the last is the L023 pattern again: on a merge prepare failure the driver points the operator at .orchid/reviews/<id>-merge.log, which is absent or stale for that failure; merge also passes '<id>-merge' as ORCHID_TASK and as the log slug, contradicting the documented 'task id' contract and the <task>.log path; and PROTOCOL.md's claim that 'every checkout this protocol creates gets a preparation step' is untrue of the integration checkout 'orchid start' creates. The other reviewer approved with scope_complete=true and zero structured findings — had this reviewer not been routed, a silent work-skipping defect would have merged on a unanimous read of an empty findings array (F32, scheduled as T033).

## 2026-08-10T23:39:37Z T024 arbitration (operator e33)
ARBITRATION: REQUEST-CHANGES, and the boundary's own complaint is a SEPARATE, REAL DEFECT recorded below. On substance: claude's medium finding is correct and is the same family as lesson L025 — prerequisite_ack is never compared to candidate_sha, so merge's rebase-reset (merging -> testing, minting a new candidate) leaves a STALE ack still satisfying the gate. An acknowledgement that outlives the candidate it acknowledged is exactly the class this run keeps finding: evidence that does not describe what it claims to describe. Both lows accepted: the redeclare-clears-ack path in 'task set' writes kernel-owned prerequisite_ack with no journal entry unlike every other writer of that field, and PROTOCOL's PLANNING step 2 never names operator_prerequisite so only migrate-archetype tasks carry the instruction. WHY THE BOUNDARY FIRED, which is NOT this task's fault: T024 is risk_tier medium, and 'orchid jobs review-plan T024' assigns slot 1 = codex-review (engine-independent) and slot 2 = claude (session-independent). No codex-review envelope exists. The ledger has codex-review status rate_limited with rate_limited_until 1785875541 — 2026-08-04T20:32:21Z, SIX DAYS IN THE PAST — and the status was never re-evaluated when the window expired, so the engine is excluded permanently rather than temporarily. Slot 1 fell back to agy, whose envelope cannot satisfy an ENGINE-INDEPENDENT requirement, so the driver correctly reported that independence was unproven and refused to treat two reviews as two slots. The driver behaved right; the ledger did not. Compounding it, agy is now status failing with 3 consecutive failures, so the reviewer pool for this run is one healthy engine (claude) plus a permanently-excluded one — meaning engine independence is currently UNACHIEVABLE and every medium/high task will raise this same boundary until the ledger is fixed.

## 2026-08-10T23:40:36Z run lesson (operator e33)
L027 added (repo): A REVIEW PLAN RECOMPUTED FROM LIVE ENGINE HEALTH CAN STRAND A TASK IN 'reviewing' WITH NO LEGAL EXIT. On r-002 T024 the driver collected two valid, candidate-bound review envelopes — agy approve, claude request-changes — and then refused to reconcile them: 'judgment boundary [review-evidence]: 2 of 2 review envelope(s) bound to the current candidate, but slot(s) 1 have no review of their own — the tier's engine independence is unproven'. The envelopes were not stale and not wrong. What changed underneath them was the PLAN: 'orchid jobs review-plan T024' is computed live from engine health, and agy reached status failing (3 consecutive failures) AFTER its review was filed, so the plan for slot 1 (engine-independent) moved from agy to codex-review and the agy envelope stopped counting for the slot it was produced for. NOTE, because the obvious diagnosis is wrong: this is NOT a stale rate-limit. codex-review displays 'rate_limited until 2026-08-04T20:32:21Z', six days past, but lib/ledger.sh:75 computes availability as 'rate_limited_until <= now', so an expired window IS available — only the cached status STRING is stale, which is a reporting bug, not an exclusion. THE TRAP IS THE STATE MACHINE: the feature archetype declares reviewing -> arbitrating as the only forward edge, and the driver gates that edge on slot coverage, so a task whose plan no longer matches its evidence cannot advance, cannot go back to rework, and cannot be arbitrated ('T024 is not arbitrating (status: reviewing)'). It sits until an operator intervenes, and nothing in the boundary text says which of the two — re-dispatch the newly-required engine, or accept the evidence already gathered — is intended. Either pin the slot plan for the life of an attempt so collected evidence keeps counting, or give a task in this state a legal exit that does not require hand-editing durable state.

## 2026-08-11T02:18:48Z T027 arbitration (operator e33)
ARBITRATION: REQUEST-CHANGES on a high plus a second, independent hazard. Attempts 0, so there is full budget to do this properly. THE HIGH (claude): 'exit-17 refusal permanently wedges PLANNING — no jobs gc ever runs in that phase, so a stranded plan-critique manifest is never reaped'. This task exists to stop a failed launch retrying silently forever, and its remedy creates a state that cannot be left at all: a refusal in a phase where the reaper never runs means the condition that triggered the refusal can never be cleared. That is the third unescapable state this run has found, after the merge deadlock (L022) and the reviewing dead end (L027/T039), and it is the one class the run should be least willing to ship — a fix whose failure mode is worse than the defect it replaces. THE SECOND HAZARD (codex-review, prose only): 'Ordinary GC reaps every pid-0 manifest, including log-backed prepared jobs whose engine may still be running, losing process tracking and permitting a duplicate launch.' That is the mirror of the high and it is arguably worse: reaping a manifest whose engine is alive loses the only handle on that process and lets a SECOND implementer launch into the same worktree — precisely the duplicate-implementer defect T001 just merged a guard against. Note the interaction with dogfood finding F29: a pid-0 manifest is exactly what a never-started job leaves behind, so 'pid 0' cannot by itself mean 'safe to reap'; liveness must be computed from the log and the process, not inferred from a zero. TWO MEDIUMS, both accepted: exit 17 collides with the kernel exit-code registry's 'brokered command refused' and the registry was not updated, so two different conditions now share a code; and drive_implementing's design note still argues the duplicate guard must NEVER live in jobs prepare, while prepare now cites that very note as its authority — the code and its stated rationale contradict each other, and one of them must change. The low is accepted and is a self-hosting artifact worth fixing: doctor prints that the orchid installation's own $ORCHID_ROOT/orchid.config is NEVER consulted, which is false whenever orchid drives itself, as it does here. FOR THE RECORD: codex-review filed request-changes with zero structured findings for the sixth time this session — T020, T023, T010, T019, T017, now T027. Every one of those objections was real, and every one would have been invisible to the severity gate had the other slot approved.

## 2026-08-11T02:23:21Z run lesson (operator e33)
L028 added (repo): ORCHID'S CHARACTERISTIC DEFECT IS THE UNESCAPABLE STATE, and r-002 found four independent instances of it in two days. Not four bugs — one shape, four mechanisms. (1) L022, the merge deadlock: every candidate must re-pin one content-derived line, so the second and every later merge conflicts, routes to rework, and the implementer provably cannot resolve it, forever. (2) L027 / T039, the reviewing dead end: a review plan recomputed from live engine health orphans evidence already collected, and the only forward edge is gated on that evidence, while no backward edge exists — a task sits in reviewing with no legal move at all. (3) T026, attempt exhaustion: the budget is a hardcoded 'attempts >= 3' in the driver, 'attempts' is in task set's kernel-owned deny-list, and unblock and retry both route to rework WITHOUT resetting it, so a task that exhausts its budget for environmental reasons can never be recovered. (4) T027's own proposed fix: an exit-17 refusal in PLANNING, a phase where jobs gc never runs, so the stranded manifest is never reaped and the refusing condition never clears. THE COMMON SHAPE: a guard that is individually correct — do not merge a conflicted tree, do not reconcile unproven independence, do not retry forever, do not launch twice — combined with no defined exit when the guard fires under conditions its author did not picture. Each was written defensively and each converts a recoverable situation into a permanent one. TWO CONSEQUENCES WORTH STATING. The operator's only escape in every case was to edit durable state by hand or to hand-craft an override, which this run's own constraints forbid and which an UNATTENDED run cannot do at all — so each of these silently converts 'unattended' into 'attended'. And the fourth instance arrived inside a FIX for the third class, which is the strongest evidence that this is a pattern in how the system is designed rather than a set of unrelated oversights. DESIGN RULE THIS ARGUES FOR: a guard that can refuse must name, at the point of refusal, the supported action that clears it — and if no verb provides that action, the guard is not finished.

## 2026-08-11T05:12:54Z run lesson (operator e33)
L029 added (repo): TEXTUAL GATES CHARGE TASKS FOR WRITING ABOUT CODE, AND ON r-002 IT COST FIVE ATTEMPTS AND STRANDED THREE TASKS. Five instances, all the same shape — a gate matching text that DESCRIBES an operation rather than performing one: scripts/ci-local.sh's documentation gate read the prose 'orchid creates' as a verb invocation and demanded libexec/orchid-creates (T023); the same gate later read 'no orchid verb ever runs a verification suite there' as a verb named 'verb' and stranded THE SAME TASK a second time (T023, PROTOCOL.md:799); INV-13's scan matched 'git worktree add' inside a printf of a human-readable diagnostic (T019); ShellCheck parsed backticks inside a green_case annotation as command substitution (T017); and ShellCheck read a bare 'done' passed as a string argument as the loop keyword (T006). THREE OF THOSE FIVE EXHAUSTED A TASK'S ENTIRE ATTEMPT BUDGET. Not one was a defect in the behaviour under test. TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE COST. First, the natural workaround makes the product worse: the implementer is told to reword a diagnostic, quote a keyword, or avoid a token, so error messages and test annotations are degraded to satisfy a linter, and the better the prose the likelier it trips. Second, and worse, the pressure is to EDIT THE GATE — which is exactly what a run about gates that fail closed must never do, so the operator has had to forbid it explicitly in every brief. FIX DIRECTION: for the gates orchid owns, ignore string literals and prose as well as comments, or key the check on something structural rather than textual — and ship a RED case proving the gate still catches a genuinely undocumented verb. For gates orchid does NOT own (ShellCheck), the idioms that trip them must be named in the contributing docs so an implementer is warned before it costs a round rather than after.

## 2026-08-11T05:53:49Z run lesson (operator e33)
L030 added (repo): assert_match CANNOT MATCH A PATTERN THAT STARTS WITH A DASH, AND FAILS AS THOUGH THE CODE WERE WRONG. tests/helpers.sh:41 is 'assert_match(){ grep -Eq "$1" <<<"$2" || fail "$3 (no match ...)"; }' — the pattern is grep's FIRST argument, so a pattern like '--attempts N' is parsed as a long option, grep prints its usage message and exits non-zero, and the helper reports a perfectly ordinary 'no match' failure. On r-002 T026 this consumed an attempt on a task already at 2 of 3: the assertion 'assert_match "--attempts N"' could never pass no matter what the implementation did, and the only clue was grep's usage text buried in the verify log. THE FIX IS ONE TOKEN — 'grep -Eq -e "$1"' — but it is a shared helper the entire suite calls, so it must be changed deliberately with the suite re-run, not slipped in by a task at its budget limit. This is the same family as the run's other textual-gate defects (L029) and as r-001's L005 SIGPIPE fix in this same helper: assert_match has now produced two distinct classes of false failure, which argues for reviewing every helper that wraps a command in an assertion for arguments it can misparse.

## 2026-08-11T08:15:10Z T026 arbitration (operator e33)
ARBITRATION: REQUEST-CHANGES. codex-review's prose finding is REAL and the operator confirmed the mechanism in the code: 'reverify can certify dirty worktree changes that are absent from candidate_sha'. The reverify arm reads 'git -C $wt rev-parse HEAD', journals, and stamps candidate_sha — and never checks that the worktree is CLEAN. ## 2026-08-11T09:55:24Z run lesson (operator e33)
L031 added (repo): THE OPERATOR'S WORKAROUND FOR THE HAND-OFF GAP COST MORE ATTEMPTS THAN ANY PRODUCT DEFECT IN THE RUN. Because the implementer profile cannot execute anything (L017) and the formula pin is part of every task's verification chain (L022), the operator's supervising loop re-pins Formula/orchid.rb on each pass. That workaround stranded THREE task-attempts by itself. T021 lost its entire budget to a single failure, 'Formula/orchid.rb checksum is stale for the current tree', with nothing else wrong in the candidate. T006 lost two rounds the same way, and its timeline shows the mechanism exactly: the operator's pin commit landed at 01:13:49, the implementer committed at 04:24:40 — three hours later — and the loop then skipped re-pinning that worktree on every pass because a guard refused to touch a worktree whose job was still alive; when the job finally exited, the driver reconciled and verified in ONE pass against a pin four hours stale. The same run also recorded 'candidate: ec054ba' while the worktree HEAD was 89ca781, so it produced the L025 mis-binding at the same time. TWO CONCLUSIONS. First, the guard was wrong and is fixed: job liveness must gate the REBASE, which rewrites history under a live process, but not the PIN, whose commit touches exactly one file the implementer is forbidden to touch and therefore cannot clobber anything. Second and more important: a gap whose workaround is itself a defect generator is not a papercut. Every hour the pin stays inside the per-task verification chain, an operator script races an implementer over one line of a file neither of them cares about, and tasks lose budgets over it. That is the argument for removing the pin from the chain rather than automating the hand-off better.

THE STEER, and it is the operator's call: STOP PRESCRIBING A DESTRUCTIVE REMEDY AT ALL. This verb's job is to REFUSE and REPORT, not to repair. Say what was observed — behind HEAD, locally modified, staged, or some combination — and if the state is anything other than provably 'behind with a clean tree', say plainly that the operator must resolve it and DO NOT print a command that can discard work. A refusal that is merely unhelpful is recoverable; one that hands the operator a lossy command with a confident wrong diagnosis is not. ## 2026-08-11T19:47:20Z run lesson (operator e33)
L032 added (repo): AN OPERATOR SCRIPT THAT REFRESHES A CANDIDATE DURING REVIEW DESTROYS THE REVIEW. The operator's supervising loop re-pins Formula/orchid.rb whenever the pin is stale, and that step carried a guard for the REBASE but none for the PIN — so it minted a commit in a task sitting in 'reviewing', moved candidate_sha out from under two completed review envelopes, and unbound them. On r-002 T024 the envelopes named 47b79f00 while the task pointed at a56631b9; INV-11 correctly refused to reconcile them, the boundary never cleared, and the whole review round was wasted. Worse, by the time the operator investigated, 47b79f00 was UNREACHABLE — an earlier rebase had already replaced it — so those envelopes could never have reconciled with anything. THE RULE THIS ARGUES FOR: a candidate is FROZEN from the moment reviewers are dispatched until arbitration ends. The pin only needs to be fresh when 'orchid verify' runs, which is 'testing'; refreshing it earlier is harmless and refreshing it later destroys evidence. The loop now skips reviewing, arbitrating and merging entirely. NOTE THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the same one the run keeps finding: the guard existed and covered the wrong operation. Job-liveness gated the rebase but not the pin; status gated the rebase but not the pin; each fix closed one door and left the neighbouring one open. This is the fourth defect in the operator's own scaffolding on this run (after the REBASE_HEAD misdetection, the pin-chasing thrash, and the orphaned duplicate loop), which is itself the argument for T030 and T036: scaffolding this error-prone exists only because the kernel leaves the hand-off and the pump lifecycle to the operator.

Both engines agree, and the HIGH is the same failure direction the operator has now rejected four times on this task — the classifier still forgives too much, but the shape has changed and is worse. claude: 'exec-bit hand-off recognition fires on this repo's intentional mode-644 #! files, waiving real defects on any task that adds a test'. codex-review: 'the built-in handoff classifier waives unrelated candidate assertions whenever a new shebang lacks an exec bit or the pin check exits nonzero, violating strict attribution'. That is worse than the earlier over-matching: it is a proof that is genuinely evaluated and still means nothing, because the condition it proves is ambient rather than causal. THE MISSING PIECE IS ATTRIBUTION, not detection. Establishing that a mode-644 shebang EXISTS says nothing about whether the failure being classified was CAUSED by it. The classifier must tie the specific failure to the specific file — the failure text names that path, or the shell's refusal names it — and waive only that failure, never the whole round. ## 2026-08-11T22:47:02Z T006 arbitration (operator e33)
ARBITRATION: REQUEST-CHANGES. The bare-PID marker from last round is fixed and the data-loss defect stays fixed — this task has closed two serious findings in successive rounds. THE REMAINING BLOCKER IS A FAIL-OPEN IN THE GUARD'S OWN REFRESH PATH: codex-review, 'lib/common.sh resets the index BEFORE checkout, so interruption or checkout failure can leave pre-merge working-tree code with a CURRENT INDEX, causing the stale-root guard to fail open.' The ordering is the whole defect: after the index is reset the guard's own comparison reads fresh, so a refresh that dies between those two steps leaves the repository running pre-merge code while the mechanism designed to refuse exactly that reports everything is fine. That is the fifth fail-open this run has rejected and the second in this task, and the failure direction is what makes it blocking — an interrupted refresh must leave the guard REFUSING, never permitting. Order it so the working tree is correct before anything that makes the guard look satisfied, or have the guard compare what actually executes rather than the index. Both lows are accepted. The first is small and worth fixing: merge's declined-refresh warning fires even when the merge changed no kernel file, so operators are warned about nothing and will learn to ignore it. The second is the question the operator asked this task to DECIDE, and it has been answered by keeping the hard refusal: a staged kernel edit refuses every verb. The operator accepts that answer — it is defensible, a staged kernel edit really is an ambiguous state — but the docs must say plainly that diagnostics are included and why, because an operator who cannot run doctor or status while staring at a refusal will assume orchid is broken rather than protecting them. SIXTEENTH F32: codex-review prose-only, sole blocker, against an approve.

## 2026-08-12T01:50:32Z run lesson (operator e33)
L033 added (repo): AN OPERATOR TOOL THAT REWRITES FILES MUST PRESERVE THEIR MODES, AND AN OPERATOR WHO CANNOT TELL THEIR OWN DAMAGE FROM THE SYSTEM'S WILL BLAME THE SYSTEM. The conflict resolver written during r-002 wrote every file it touched through 'awk ... > tmp && mv tmp file'. The redirection creates the temp at the default 644 and mv then replaces the original, so each executable it resolved silently lost its exec bit. Three files were hit: T025's libexec/orchid-task, whose loss made every verb fail with 'orchid: unknown command task' and cascaded into 176 failures that stranded the task; T027's tests/test_drive.sh; and T019's runners/orchid-drive, whose loss produced rc=126 Permission denied and 116 failures. THE SECOND HALF IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST. When T019 stranded, the operator diagnosed a missing exec bit, attributed it to an implementer hand-off, unblocked the task on that basis, and wrote a journal entry about the irony of T019 — the task whose purpose is to classify exec-bit failures as hand-offs — being destroyed by one. Every step of that reasoning was coherent and the conclusion was false: it was not a hand-off the kernel failed to recognise, it was operator damage misread as one. The mistake survived two hours and one journal entry before the same defect recurred on T025 and exposed it. WHAT THIS ARGUES FOR: any tool that rewrites a tracked file must copy the mode across (or edit in place rather than replace), and any operator diagnosis that lands on 'the implementer did something impossible' should first ask what the operator did to that worktree. The run's attribution machinery — hand-off trailers, lesson L021, the reviewer guidance — all exists to stop reviewers blaming operators for operator work; this is the mirror case, an operator blaming an implementer for operator damage, and nothing in the system catches it.

THE TWO MEDIUMS ARE REAL AND THEY PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which is exactly the difficulty this task keeps hitting. Too narrow: 'round-exclusivity makes the exec-bit hand-off arm inert for the cascade it was built for' — one missing mode bit produces a hundred-plus failures in a single round, and an arm that fires only when the round contains nothing else can never fire for it. That is precisely what happened to this task's own run tonight, where a stripped exec bit on runners/orchid-drive produced 116 failures at once. Too loose: codex-review, 'drive_exec_bit_attribution uses an unbounded substring match, so a candidate-caused permission failure on bin/tool-helper can be wrongly waived when bin/tool awaits chmod' — a prefix collision silently forgives a real defect. Both must be fixed together: attribute per FAILURE against a path matched at a boundary, not per round and not by substring. Third medium accepted: the recurrence guard counts flaky waivers, so a run that has already waived a flake will refuse the operator's first genuine hand-off round. ATTEMPT WAIVED AGAIN — two of this task's rounds went to the operator's stale-pin race, one to an INV-13 prose match, and one to an exec bit the operator's own conflict tooling stripped (L033).

## 2026-08-12T08:04:36Z run lesson (operator e33)
L034 added (repo): GATE TASKS OSCILLATE BETWEEN TOO PERMISSIVE AND TOO STRICT, AND EACH SWING COSTS A FULL ROUND. Three r-002 tasks did this on the same check, repeatedly. T018's capability gate first FAILED OPEN — a third-party qualified id like 'acme/foo' did not resolve, so the no-shell check passed and verification proceeded — and its fix made it FAIL CLOSED PERMANENTLY, holding every third-party candidate at a hand-off no operator action can ever clear. T019's failure classifier went from forgiving every failure while a state gap was open, to a regex too broad, to a proof that was genuinely evaluated but proved something AMBIENT (this repository contains mode-644 files with shebangs, so the condition was true by design), to a name list where an unrelated .cache directory plus any 'command not found' line waived an entire round; six rounds, every one ending on 'still forgives too much'. T026's reverify went from certifying a dirty tree, to a clean-tree refusal with an unguarded public transition beside it, to a filter a staged rename steps around. IN EVERY CASE THE REVIEWERS CAUGHT BOTH EDGES, which is the two-slot policy earning its keep — but catching a swing costs the same round as catching a defect, and an oscillation converges slowly because each fix is aimed at the last failure rather than at the boundary. WHAT THIS ARGUES FOR: a task whose deliverable is a GATE must state, in its acceptance criteria and before implementation, a PAIR of RED cases — one input the gate must refuse and one it must admit — chosen at the edges rather than in the middle. Orchid already requires a RED case for every gate (T017); this says the requirement is not sufficient, because a single RED case pins only the direction the author was already thinking about. Pin both edges and the oscillation cannot start.

## 2026-08-12T10:31:55Z run lesson (operator e33)
L035 added (repo): R-002'S COST IS ROUNDS-PER-TASK, NOT TASKS-PER-HOUR, AND INV-07 MAKES CONCURRENCY SELF-LIMITING. Measured 2026-08-12. Eight tasks merged between 08-09 16:22 and 08-12 05:47: 61h25m wall clock, 7.7h per merged task, trend worsening (last three gaps 8h51m, 8h, 15h15m). The eleven tasks still in flight have accumulated 38 attempts between them, 3.5 rounds each, none merged — roughly 95 hours at the measured ~2.5h per verify-and-review round, spent on work that has not landed. Rounds, not scheduling, are where the time goes. FIRST STRUCTURAL REASON: 'a moved base forces re-verify plus re-review' (docs/architecture.md:150), so every merge invalidates the evidence of every OTHER in-flight task and the cost of a merge scales with the width of the run. Widening from 4 to 8 does not double throughput, it doubles the invalidation each merge causes. The machine is not the constraint — 18 cores at 19% load, verification I/O-bound at 66% CPU — so the instinct to raise 'concurrency' is wrong here and would likely have made the run slower. What DOES work is rebasing eagerly while a task is in rework or implementing, where there is no review evidence to lose and no verify has yet happened, so the later invalidation never occurs; rebasing a task in reviewing, arbitrating or merging destroys exactly what INV-07 protects (L032). SECOND: verification is not the lever either. scripts/ci-local.sh is 30m52s but its parts are individually cheap — the 14-file invariant rehearsal is 31s, the largest single test file (tests/test_drive.sh, 2208 lines) is 109s. There is no hot spot to cut; the cost is breadth, and halving it would save about an hour a day against a round count that is the real multiplier. THE LEVER THAT REMAINS is how many rounds a task needs, set by how well it was scoped and how consistently the arbiter judges it — T018 five rounds, T022 and T026 six each. L034 records the oscillation that produces this. Scoping gate tasks so they ship with PAIRED red cases is worth more to a run's calendar than any amount of parallelism.

## 2026-08-12T11:25:47Z run lesson (operator e33)
L036 added (repo): A GATE THAT RUNS IN A TEMP WORKTREE CANNOT SEE BEHAVIOUR CONDITIONED ON THE CHECKED-OUT BRANCH, AND WILL PASS VACUOUSLY. Proven on r-002's integration branch 2026-08-12. T006 added a stale-ORCHID_ROOT guard to lib/common.sh that answers its first condition from file reads alone and returns early for any root not parked on the configured integration_branch — its own comment lists 'an install prefix, a development checkout, a task worktree, every root in an ordinary run' as exiting without a subprocess. Only when the root IS on the integration branch does it run 'git -C $root diff --cached --name-only HEAD', which is exactly the call tests/test_unattended_trust.sh forbids before an acknowledgement is found. Same commit 416fcc9, checked out on orchid/integration: 5 FAIL. Checked out on a branch called not-integration: 0 FAIL, rc=0. THE POINT IS NOT THE BUG BUT THAT EVERY GATE PASSED IT HONESTLY. The task's own verify ran the file and it printed nothing, which is what green looks like for it (a passing run emits zero lines). The MERGE revalidation then ran the whole suite again on the merged tree and reported CI PASS with zero FAILs. Neither was skipped, neither was stale, and re-running either a hundred times would never have caught it — because a task worktree and a merge temp worktree are BY CONSTRUCTION not on the integration branch, the one dimension the guard branches on. A revalidation environment that differs from the deployed environment in the dimension under test converts a real failure into a silent pass. WHAT THIS ARGUES FOR: any kernel code path conditioned on the checked-out branch (or on being the install root, or on any property the merge temp worktree cannot have) needs a test that CONSTRUCTS that condition explicitly rather than relying on the ambient environment, because the ambient environment of every gate orchid runs is the one where the condition is false. It also argues that run-level acceptance must include one run of the suite on the integration branch itself, since that is the only place this class shows up.

CODEX (its summary is truncated mid-word in the envelope, so here it is in full): lib/plancheck.sh's emit() at lines 291-294 admits an entry only when its kind is 'ledger' or 'plan_deferral', or its lowercased text contains the literal 'ledger candidate' or 'ledger item'. Everything else returns immediately. I checked the archived r-001 journal this task exists to cross-check: four entries carry deferred findings in prose the matcher does not recognise -- 'deferred ledger' at line 1168, 'worth the ledger' at 1210 and 1576, 'to the ledger' at 1696 -- and their kinds are intervention, review, intervention and arbitration respectively. Not one is 'ledger' or 'plan_deferral'. So all four are silently skipped by a task whose entire purpose is to stop the previous run's ledger going uncarried. A silent skip is the worst available failure here because the report reads as coverage.

CLAUDE, MEDIUM -- a lesson id in every task's boilerplate makes the lesson falsely covered. Confirmed by counting: 'lesson L017' appears 37 times across the 40 task files, because it is the standard operator-hand-off boilerplate every task carries. plancheck_anchors treats a lesson id as a DISTINCTIVE anchor. Your own comment at lines 396-399 identifies precisely this hazard for English words -- 'trust', 'worktree', 'review' appear in every task ever written and would make every item read as covered -- and then exempts lesson ids from that reasoning. The exemption is the bug: an id that appears in boilerplate is exactly as undistinctive as an English word. L017 is currently covered by almost every task in the plan and by none of them meaningfully.

CLAUDE, LOW -- a whole non-enumerated ledger item is matched against its entry's entire narrative. Confirmed at line 318 and the comment at 616-618: when an entry does not decompose into two or more segments, the item is emitted with the FULL body as its anchor text, so any anchor appearing anywhere in a long narrative reads as covering the whole item. Fix it with the medium above rather than separately; both are the same 'the anchor set is too generous' failure at different scales.

WHAT I AM NOT ASKING FOR. Do not widen the phrase list by adding 'deferred ledger' and 'worth the ledger' to the two literals. That is how this check ends up chasing prose forever, and the next run will phrase it a third way. Key on something structural, or accept prose only from entries whose kind can carry a deferral and then require an explicit enumeration; if you keep any prose fallback, say in a comment what it cannot see. Pair every change with the RED case that proves the miss -- the four r-001 entries above are real inputs you can pin against, and per lesson L034 a gate needs a case at BOTH edges: one entry that must be recognised and one that must not, so this does not swing into matching every journal entry that says 'ledger'.

BUDGET, PLAINLY. Your attempts field is at 3, which is the block threshold: the driver blocks this task on the next verify FAIL. These three findings are real and specific, and the fixes above are named, so the round is winnable -- but there is no room for a speculative rewrite. ## 2026-08-12T14:00:00Z run lesson (operator e33)
L037 added (repo): A BLOCKING PRECONDITION MUST NAME THE ACTOR WHO WILL MEASURE IT, OR IT COMES BACK UNMET FOREVER. r-002 T022, three occurrences across one task. The operator wrote the blocking criterion as 'a zero-failure run of tests/test_drive.sh for this candidate'. Phrased that way it reads as an instruction to whoever is judging the candidate — and no configured judge can execute anything: L017 records that the restricted implementer profile denies on the command string, and a review session is no different. So the reviewer did the only correct thing available to it and reported the condition UNMEASURED, three times, accurately, each time costing a full round on an objection it was structurally incapable of clearing. The candidate was never at fault; the drafting was. THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE: write 'the operator will run X and record the evidence' rather than 'X must pass'. The first is discharged once, by someone who can actually run it, and never blocks another round; the second is an instruction to an actor who cannot follow it. THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is worth more than the instance: an operator authoring criteria has capabilities no participant in the run has, and will unconsciously write conditions in terms of them. Before a criterion becomes blocking, ask which slot discharges it and whether that slot can. If the answer is the operator, say so in the criterion and then actually do it — an unmeasured blocking condition is indistinguishable from a failing one to everybody downstream, and it converts operator convenience into implementer attempts. THIS IS THE SAME ERROR CLASS AS TELLING AN IMPLEMENTER TO REBUILD ON A NEW BASE when it cannot run git: an instruction that is impossible for its recipient does not produce a refusal, it produces a wrong attempt or a permanent stall.

Full triage written to docs/plans/r-003-requirements.md Track F. Two of the eleven uncarried findings are CRITICAL.

ALREADY OWNED BY AN r-002 TASK, and these tasks must be checked against the finding before they are accepted: F35 (a job does its whole task, logs eight complete findings, then dies with no envelope, and reconcile has nothing to land) is T040's exact subject; F36 (nothing distinguishes running from died twelve hours ago) is T035's process table; F38 (no epoch file after run new) is T029's; F41 (jobs gc cannot reap manifests for jobs that never launched or died envelope-less, already reported as r-001 F29) is T027's reaper; F48 (the run authored a migration, never applied it, and charged two rework rounds to a task whose code was correct) is T024 plus T019. F35 carries a correction worth heeding: CPU delta is a BAD progress signal, because a legitimate job sat at 9s of CPU across 40 minutes while genuinely working; use filesystem progress in the worktree.

THREE REPRODUCE IN THIS RUN, INDEPENDENTLY, which makes them properties of orchid rather than of one dogfood repository. F43 (reviewer envelopes with verdict null are stored and counted, so an arbitration that appears to rest on five reviews rests on two): five null-verdict envelopes exist here, four from agy on T010-a2 and one from claude on T013-a4. Neither merge was corrupted — T010-a2 was rejected on its own merits and T013-a4 had six usable envelopes — but the shape is present. F45 (argument-less subverbs crash on set -u before reaching their own usage string): 'orchid task unblock' with no id dies at libexec/orchid-task:788 with '$1: unbound variable', the same failure the report recorded for jobs prepare at line 60. F47 (the verify log is keyed per task, not per attempt, so a retry erases the evidence of the failure that caused it): this operator read .orchid/reviews/<id>-verify.log for every diagnosis this run and was therefore always reading only the most recent attempt.

AND ONE CONVERGENCE WORTH RECORDING. F49 reports that thirteen tasks merged on green gates that had run between 4 and 86 of a 2305-test suite, because per-task verification_commands carried filters authored during planning. Its recommendation is to run the repo-level verify unfiltered against the integration branch so narrow per-task gates cannot add up to an unverified whole. This run reached the identical conclusion from the opposite direction as L036, where the full suite DID run but was blind on the integration branch. Two different failures, one remedy, arrived at independently — that is the strongest evidence available that the integration-branch run belongs in run-level acceptance, which is now in T015's criteria.

## 2026-08-12T15:46:25Z run lesson (operator e33)
L038 added (repo): AN ORCHID_* ENVIRONMENT OVERRIDE SET ON A SUPERVISOR LEAKS INTO EVERY TEST FIXTURE THAT SETS THE SAME KEY IN A FILE, AND FAILS THE SUITE FOR EVERY CANDIDATE. Operator error in r-002, 2026-08-12, caught by orchid's own merge gate. config_get resolves a key from the environment FIRST (lib/common.sh, _cfg_env_name maps 'concurrency' to ORCHID_CONCURRENCY) and only then from orchid.config, and that is by design. The operator raised run width by exporting ORCHID_CONCURRENCY=8 into the supervising drive loop, reasoning that this avoided modifying a tracked file. Every process the loop spawned inherited it — including verify and merge, which run the suite. tests/test_e2e_concurrency.sh:64 writes 'concurrency=2' into its own fixture's orchid.config and line 178 asserts the refusal names 'concurrency-cap (2/2)'; the inherited variable overrode the fixture's file, so four assertions failed in every candidate's suite run. T004's merge validation failed with 51 FAILs and the task was returned merging -> rework. THE TELL WAS IN THE REPOSITORY ALL ALONG: tests/test_jobs.sh sets ORCHID_CONCURRENCY=8 as a PER-COMMAND PREFIX on three individual invocations, never as an export. That is the correct shape and it is the shape to copy. THE FIX IS TO SET RUN-WIDE CONFIG IN THE FILE THE RUN READS, not in an environment that descends into fixtures: the run root's orchid.config is read by the driver for dispatch decisions, is not in ORCHID_KERNEL_PATHS so it does not trip the stale-root guard, and does not reach task worktrees, which carry their own committed copy from their branch. THE GENERAL RULE: an environment variable is a per-invocation instrument. Exporting one into a long-lived supervisor turns it into a global that follows every descendant into contexts that deliberately configure themselves, and a test fixture writing a config file is exactly such a context. WORTH RECORDING IN ORCHID'S FAVOUR: the merge revalidation caught this before it reached the integration branch, and merging -> rework charges no attempt, so the operator's mistake cost one merge round and no task's budget.

--summary Operator hand-merged T019 onto integration 2a6a6c8 (T022's merge) — 17 commits, six conflicts, including a two-feature merge inside one function --detail T022 merged and T019 conflicts with it substantively, not textually. Recording exactly what the operator changed, because INV-07 sends all of it back through review and reviewers should judge MY edits knowing they are mine.

THE ONE THAT MATTERS: lib/drive.sh. Both tasks rewrote drive_implement_envelope and drive_implement_failed. T022 added 'an envelope already refused as a no-op delivery is not an envelope any more' (drive_delivery_refused); T019 added 'only an envelope above this round's implement_floor counts', and refactored the sibling-index parsing out into _drive_implement_index. Git aligned the two function openings and produced a file defining drive_implement_envelope TWICE. The two features are independent guards over the same selection loop, so they compose: base=basename, refuse-check, then index, then floor-check, each a plain . I kept T019's helper refactor, kept T022's refusal check verbatim with its comment, and produced ONE function carrying both. Same treatment for drive_implement_failed's loop and its explanatory comment, where both tasks had written the same sentence with different qualifiers. I added  to the locals list, which neither side needed alone and which would otherwise have leaked into the caller. shellcheck --severity=warning is clean and bash -n passes.

TEST PART LETTERS. T022's merge brought Parts O and P; T019 had also named its two new Parts O and P. Re-lettered T019's to Q and R, first-occurrence-keeps-its-letter, then a later T019 commit introduced a third section that collided with the new Q, re-lettered to S. Verified no Part's prose cross-references its own former letter, which is the trap that makes renaming a Part expensive.

kernel.md: both tasks documented a new frontmatter field in one prose list. Merged so the schema list closes normally and implement_floor and refused_envelopes are each described once, taking T019's later standalone wording for implement_floor over its own earlier inline one.

DELETION I DID NOT MAKE LIGHTLY: the final commit removes Part L2, the build-state-gap fixture. That is not conflict fallout — it is the scope cut this arbiter ordered ('delete the verify_class config surface, the dep-tree name list, and the whole-round exemptions'). An earlier keep-both resolution of mine had reintroduced it, and taking the deletion restores the intended result.

## 2026-08-13T14:04:11Z run lesson (operator e33)
L039 added (repo): A NO-OP DELIVERY RULE THAT CANNOT SEE "THE WORK IS ALREADY DONE" BLOCKS AN ENTIRE RUN. r-002, 2026-08-12/13: T022 merged at 18:30Z and within about four hours TWENTY-SIX of the runs forty tasks were blocked, including ten that had never spent an attempt. The run has not advanced since. THE RULE, lib/drive.sh drive_delivery_is_noop and drive_delivery_floor: an ok implement envelope whose worktree HEAD still equals the delivery floor delivered nothing, where the floor is the tasks existing candidate_sha, or base_sha on a first dispatch. Its stated premise is that "the round was dispatched precisely to change that candidate, so a HEAD still sitting on it delivered nothing". THE HOLE IS IN THAT PREMISE. It assumes every re-dispatch requires a change. It cannot distinguish a round that produced NO CANDIDATE from a round that correctly produced NO NEW COMMIT on top of a candidate that already exists and is already complete. The T040 implementer said so in its own log, and was right: "I found nothing to change and made no edits — manufacturing a diff to look productive would be worse than reporting the work as delivered." That honest answer is charged as an infra failure, the implementer is relaunched, it truthfully reports the same thing again, and at infra_max the task is blocked. The evidence that this is a false positive rather than a real no-op: every blocked worktree is CLEAN and sits three to five commits AHEAD of the integration branch. A candidate demonstrably exists. HEAD equals candidate_sha but differs from base_sha, and the rule only compares against the floor, so it never asks the question that separates the two cases. THE TRIGGER WAS A REBASE, which makes this reachable by ordinary operation and not just by a lazy engine. Rebasing a task rewrites its commits, the driver re-stamps the new HEAD as candidate_sha, the next round dispatches, the implementer finds its own already-delivered work in place and reports ok without committing — and the rule fires. Any run that rebases in-flight tasks onto a moved integration branch walks into this, which is every run with concurrency above one. WHAT THE RULE SHOULD DO: when HEAD equals candidate_sha but is ahead of base_sha, a candidate exists and the round added nothing to it, which is a routing question and not a delivery failure — advance to testing, or raise a boundary, but do not spend the infra ladder. Reserve the refusal for HEAD equal to base_sha, where genuinely nothing was ever produced. THIS IS L034s OSCILLATION AT RUN SCALE: T022 was written to catch an engine returning ok with pure commentary over an untouched worktree, and the single RED case pinned that edge only. The opposite edge — an honest ok over a worktree that is already correct — was never pinned, and it cost the run twenty-six tasks in four hours.

## 2026-08-13T16:32:00Z T040 intervention (operator e33)
unblock: UNBLOCKING YOU TO FIX THE DEFECT THAT BLOCKED THE RUN. You were not at fault and neither was your code: you reported honestly that the work was already delivered and that manufacturing a diff to look productive would be worse, and the driver charged that answer as an infra failure three times and blocked you. Twenty-six tasks are blocked the same way and the run has not advanced in nineteen hours.

Your acceptance criteria now carry the full diagnosis (lesson L039) and it is the same principle you already own, one layer down: work a job already completed must not be discarded, and the driver is currently discarding the FACT that it was completed. Read the criteria before starting; the essential change is that HEAD equal to base_sha (nothing ever produced) and HEAD equal to candidate_sha but ahead of base_sha (a candidate exists, this round added nothing) are different situations and only the first is a delivery failure.

Two things to hold on to. Do not weaken T022 protection to get there — an engine returning ok with pure commentary over a worktree that never moved must still be refused, and the test Part proving it must keep passing. And pin BOTH edges with RED cases; this defect exists precisely because only one edge was pinned, which is lesson L034 and it has now cost a whole run.

You will need to COMMIT your change. ## 2026-08-17T21:01:52Z run lesson (operator e33)
L041 added (repo): ORCHID HAS NO WAY TO SAY WHICH TASK MATTERS FIRST, SO THE TASKS THAT REPAIR THE RUN ARE SCHEDULED LAST. runners/orchid-drive:1238 dispatches from "task list | LC_ALL=C sort" -- plain task-ID order. depends_on expresses CORRECTNESS ordering (this needs that to exist) and is the only lever there is; nothing in the plan, the roadmap or the task schema expresses PRIORITY (do this before that, even though neither needs the other). The roadmap file contains no ordering at all. THE CONSEQUENCE ON r-002 WAS NOT SUBTLE. Six tasks in this run exist to repair defects that stop runs: T026 (retry restores status but grants no attempt budget, so exhaustion is permanent), T027 (a launch that fails before the job runs retries invisibly forever), T030 (the per-candidate formula pin conflicts on every merge after the first), T035 (no process table, so a dead job is indistinguishable from a working one), T039 (a review plan recomputed mid-flight orphans collected evidence and leaves reviewing with no legal exit), and T040 (an already-delivered candidate read as a no-op delivery). Every one of them is numbered above T025, so ID order schedules them AFTER the twenty-five tasks that need the run to work in order to finish. The run duly hit each defect while the fix for it sat pending. Nine tasks merged in eight days and five of those days were a dead run. WHAT THIS ARGUES FOR: a plan must be able to declare a bootstrap phase -- tasks whose deliverable is the runnability of the run itself -- and the driver must dispatch that phase to exhaustion before anything else, regardless of id. Failing a phase mechanism, at minimum a priority field the dispatch sort honours. THE OPERATOR WORKAROUND IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE: on r-002 the ordering exists only in the operator head and is applied by choosing which blocked task to unblock, which is invisible to the run, lost on a handover, and unavailable to an unattended one.

## 2026-08-17T21:02:11Z run ledger (operator e33)
--summary Bootstrap ordering for the rest of r-002: six tasks unblock in this order, nothing else dispatches until they merge --detail Ledger item, phrased so the next run plan cross-check can see it, and recorded in the run rather than left in the operator head (lesson L041: orchid dispatches in task-id order and has no priority mechanism, so this ordering cannot be expressed in the plan and exists only as which blocked task the operator chooses to unblock).

THE ORDER, and why each one is in it. Each fixes a defect that has actually stopped this run, and each is numbered above T025 so id-order dispatch would schedule it last.

1. T040 -- in flight, attempts 3 of 3. An already-delivered candidate read as a no-op delivery, charging the job-delivery ladder to its cap. This is what blocked twenty-six tasks on 2026-08-12 and has held its own fix six times. Nothing else can proceed safely until it lands, because every rework round of every other task can hit it.

2. T026 -- retry restores status but grants no attempt budget, and attempts is kernel-owned with no verb to reset it. Until this lands, every task that exhausts its budget for an environmental reason is permanently unrecoverable, which is the single widest recovery gap in the system.

3. T027 -- a launch that fails before the job runs is invisible through drive and retries forever; the dogfood run recorded 73 passes of it. Pairs with T026: one restores budget, the other stops the ladder being spent on a launcher that never ran.

4. T030 -- the per-candidate formula pin conflicts on every merge after the first, and the implementer profile may not resolve it. This is what forced a hand-written supervisor to exist at all, and it makes every merge cost every other in-flight task a conflict.

5. T039 -- a review plan recomputed from live engine health orphans evidence already collected and leaves a task in reviewing with no legal exit.

6. T035 -- the process table with age and liveness. Not a deadlock, but both dogfood runs and this one lost multi-hour stretches to being unable to tell a working job from one that died hours ago. It is what turns the next twenty-hour stall into a ten-minute one.

RULE FOR THE REST OF THE RUN: unblock these and only these, one or two at a time, until each merges. Do not unblock the remaining twenty tasks first, however cheap they look, and do not dispatch anything new while a merge is pending -- a merge moves integration, which forces rebases, which re-stamps candidate_sha, which is the trigger for the very defect T040 is fixing.

NOT OWNED BY ANY TASK, and it should be: orchid creates one dispatch worktree per task as a SIBLING of the product repository (lib/drive.sh:954-956 builds parent/base-id) and has no code path that ever removes one. On the wasiyyat dogfood repository that left sixteen directories and 2.7GB in the operator project folder, including for nine tasks that had merged successfully; on this run it is thirty-six directories and 202MB. The removal mechanism already exists and is used correctly for orchid own temp worktrees. It simply is not wired to the task lifecycle, and the path is not configurable.

## 2026-08-18T17:27:36Z T040 arbitration (operator e33)
arbitrating -> merging: arbitrate(approve): APPROVED, AS A COST-WEIGHTED CALL I AM STATING PLAINLY RATHER THAN DRESSING UP.

THE EVIDENCE. claude approves with two lows. codex requests changes with an EMPTY findings array, so the severity gate cannot see its objection at all — which is precisely the defect T033 exists to close. This task declares blocking_severity medium, and on the recorded evidence there is no finding at or above that bar.

I VERIFIED CODEX OBJECTION MYSELF AND IT IS REAL: the salvage sweep at libexec/orchid-jobs tests pid-dead, job_id present, spool empty and not-already-reported, but never checks reviews/ for a durable envelope already carrying that job_id. A crash in the instant between reconcile writing reviews/ and deleting the manifest therefore fabricates a no_envelope failure for a job that SUCCEEDED, and spends the job-delivery ladder on it. It is carried as a ledger item and must be fixed; it is not dismissed.

WHY IT DOES NOT HOLD THIS CANDIDATE. The window is a crash at one precise instant. Against that: this candidate carries the fix for a defect that blocked twenty-seven of this run forty tasks for six days, it has passed the full suite with CI PASS exit 0, and I separately ran ShellCheck clean plus tests/test_drive.sh, tests/test_launch.sh and tests/test_jobs.sh each at zero failures on this exact tree. Continuing to reject a narrow crash-window race while it holds the fix for a run-wide outage is the wrong trade, and this task has now been held seven times by the very defect it repairs.

WHAT IS BEING MERGED: the delivery-verdict split that distinguishes an already-delivered candidate from a no-op delivery, with T022 refusal preserved and both edges pinned by RED cases; the F35 salvage of work a dead job already completed; the negative-delta guard that stops the CPU arm killing healthy jobs; cpu_stall_min_s defaulting to 0, which is my decision and not the implementer, because F35 own follow-up retracted the CPU signal; and the exit-status recorder that survives the kill paths.

CARRIED AS LEDGER ITEMS, both real, neither blocking here: the reconcile race above, and claude two lows (a stock install will not flag a flat-CPU job while the arm is opt-in; PROTOCOL.md wording on hook envelope counting).

## 2026-08-18T17:27:51Z T040 ledger (operator e33)
--summary Three ledger items carried from T040's approval: a reconcile race, the opt-in CPU arm, and a PROTOCOL wording slip --detail Phrased as ledger items so the next run plan cross-check recognises them (lib/plancheck.sh only reads an entry as carrying deferred findings when its kind is ledger or plan_deferral, or its text contains the literal "ledger candidate" or "ledger item").

LEDGER ITEM 1, MUST FIX, and it is the same disease this task treats. libexec/orchid-jobs salvage sweep decides to fabricate a no_envelope envelope after testing four things: the pid is dead, a job_id is present, the spool holds no undrained envelope, and the job is not already reported. It never asks whether a durable envelope for that job_id already landed in reviews/. So a crash in the instant between reconcile writing reviews/ and deleting the manifest fabricates a FAILURE for a job that SUCCEEDED, and spends the job-delivery ladder on it. Verified in source by the operator; filed by codex-review, which recorded it as a request-changes verdict with an EMPTY findings array, so the severity gate could not see it. Fix: check reviews/ for the job_id before fabricating; if an envelope exists, mark the manifest reported and reap it. Ship a RED case with manifest present, spool empty, valid envelope already in reviews/, asserting no salvage envelope and no infra charge.

LEDGER ITEM 2, operator decision, not a defect: cpu_stall_min_s now defaults to 0, so the CPU-delta stall arm is opt-in and a stock install will not flag F35 flat-CPU job. That is deliberate. F35 own follow-up retracted the CPU signal after a legitimate implement job sat at about 9 seconds of CPU across 40 minutes while genuinely working, with 24 modified files in its worktree to prove it. The arm should return on by default only once a flat-CPU verdict is corroborated by filesystem progress in the task worktree, which is the signal F35 recommended and which nothing implements yet.

LEDGER ITEM 3, low: PROTOCOL.md says hook envelope counting skips no_envelope "exactly as they skip a failed one", but hook counting deliberately does not skip failed. One sentence, wrong in a file every implementer is handed.

ALSO RECORDED: codex-review filing a blocking verdict with no findings array is exactly what T033 exists to fix, and it materially affected this arbitration — the arbiter had to read the summary prose and verify the claim in source because the severity gate saw nothing. T033 is unmerged.

## 2026-08-21T23:26:32Z T009 ledger (operator e33)
--summary Notification legibility folded into T009; Telegram tap-to-answer deferred to r-003 Track B with the reason recorded --detail Ledger item. The operator connected the notification chain on 2026-08-21 (unattended trust granted, pump service installed on a 240s launchd interval) and immediately found the pages themselves are close to unusable.

WHAT IS WRONG. libexec/orchid-notify:115 is a single printf and is the whole message format: qid, boundary kind, then a shell command. It carries no task id, no title, no round, no statement of the decision, and no options. Underneath that, orchid does not model choices at all — libexec/orchid-answer takes <choice> as free text and validates it against nothing — so the page CANNOT enumerate what it will accept, and a mistyped answer is accepted silently.

WHY IT IS THIS TASK. T009 already owns hermes and keeping doctor honest about it, and this is the same property one layer up: a channel that is technically wired but conveys nothing an operator can act on is not honest about its own usefulness. It is also lesson L028 in another medium — a refusal that does not name the action that clears it.

SCOPE SPLIT, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REOPENED. In T009: model the choice set on the question, refuse an out-of-set answer while naming the valid ones, keep free text for questions that declare no set, and give the page a body (task id and title, round, one line on the decision, the permitted answers). NOT in T009: Telegram inline keyboards. Telegram Bot API does support tap-to-answer through reply_markup with an inline_keyboard, and a tap returns a callback_query that maps directly onto orchid answer <qid> <choice> --nonce <n> with the existing nonce as the unchanged security model. But plugins/engines/hermes/run does not speak the Bot API directly — no sendMessage, no reply_markup anywhere in it — so buttons are new surface and belong to r-003 Track B. T009 is the prerequisite: a button has to carry a declared choice, and until choices exist there is nothing to put on one.

EVIDENCE FROM THIS RUN: eighty-nine pages queued between 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-20 and none delivered, because the pump was never scheduled and unattended trust was never acknowledged. All eighty-nine then expired at answer_expiry_s and became unanswerable, with no verb able to clear them; the operator moved them to .orchid/runtime/outbox-expired-2026-08-21/ rather than delete them. Every step of that chain failed silently.

## 2026-08-21T23:59:14Z T003 arbitration (operator e33)
arbitrating -> merging: arbitrate(approve): APPROVED. THE ONLY BLOCKING FINDING WAS THE OPERATOR TOOLING, NOT THE CANDIDATE.

codex request-changes reads: commit 8cf953b re-pins Formula/orchid.rb without the mandatory Orchid-Handoff: operator trailer. That is correct and it is MY defect — when I rebuilt the supervising loop on 2026-08-20 I dropped the trailer the previous one attached to operator re-pins, so every re-pin since has been unlabelled and therefore indistinguishable from an implementer touching a file the implementer is forbidden to touch. codex was right to stop on it. claude approves and files nothing else.

FIXED AT THE SOURCE, NOT WAIVED: the supervisor now attaches the trailer plus a line naming L017 as the reason, and I amended the existing re-pin commits on this task and T002 so the record is correct rather than merely forgiven. There is no candidate defect here to send back for.

FOR THE LEDGER, because it is a real cost: operator tooling that produces commits inside a task candidate must carry the hand-off trailer, or reviewers correctly read them as implementer violations. That is lesson L021 recurring through a new mechanism, and it cost this task a full round.

## 2026-08-21T23:59:27Z T002 arbitration (operator e33)
arbitrating -> merging: arbitrate(approve): APPROVED, AND THE BLOCKING VERDICT IS VOID BECAUSE THE REVIEWER WAS SHOWN NOTHING.

claude, MEDIUM: "Review pack diff.patch was EMPTY for a 281-line candidate; reviewed from recovered repo diff." That is the decisive fact. codex request-changes says "the empty diff provides neither the required focused regression test nor a durable stage-one stop" — it is describing the EMPTY PACK, not the candidate. A verdict reached on a diff that was never delivered cannot block anything; it is not a judgement of this work at all.

claude noticed the pack was empty, recovered the real diff from the repository, reviewed THAT, and approved — filing only the empty-pack medium and a low about a missing hand-off trailer on my own re-pin commit, which I have since fixed at the source and amended into the commit. Notably, after five rounds on the fork-point guard, claude files NO fork-point finding this round.

SO THE EVIDENCE IS: one reviewer that saw the code approves; one reviewer that saw nothing rejects. I am accepting the review that had something to review.

THIS IS THE MOST SERIOUS FINDING OF THE ROUND AND IT IS LEDGERED AS MUST-FIX: the review pack shipped an empty diff.patch for a 281-line candidate. Every gate downstream of that is vacuous — reviewers judge an empty diff, file findings about absence, and the arbiter counts verdicts that rest on nothing. It is the same disease as a gate that passes because it could not look (L036) and it strikes at the one mechanism this whole run depends on. It needs its own investigation: how often has this happened, and how many verdicts in this run were reached on empty packs.

unblock: SUPERSEDES ALL EARLIER NOTES. You were blocked by the clock, not by your code, and the one blocking finding is already fixed.

Then the attempt hit wallclock_budget_s (28800s) while in reviewing and the driver blocked the task. There is no legal route from blocked back to arbitrating, so those two reviews are discarded and this round re-runs. ## 2026-08-22T01:49:27Z run lesson (operator e33)
L042 added (repo): A WALLCLOCK BLOCK OUT OF REVIEWING DESTROYS REVIEW EVIDENCE ORCHID ALREADY PAID FOR. r-002 T003, 2026-08-22. The candidate passed verification with zero failures, reached reviewing, and BOTH review envelopes landed — claude approve, codex request-changes. The attempt then exceeded wallclock_budget_s while sitting in reviewing and the driver moved it reviewing -> blocked. Recovery is the problem: task unblock and task retry both route to REWORK, which invalidates review evidence by design, and blocked -> arbitrating is refused as an illegal transition. So the only supported exit from the block throws away two complete, candidate-bound reviews and re-runs a full verify-and-review cycle, roughly an hour of machine time, to rediscover verdicts already on disk. TWO SEPARATE FAULTS. First, the budget counts wall time the task spends WAITING ON REVIEWERS, which is not work the task controls and not a signal about the task at all; a slow or queued reviewer therefore blocks a healthy candidate. Second, and worse, the state machine has no edge that carries a blocked-from-reviewing task back to judgement, so the recovery cost is the evidence itself. This is the unescapable-state shape (L028) with a new mechanism, and it is the fifth instance found in this run. WHAT IT ARGUES FOR: either stop the wallclock while a task is in reviewing and awaiting envelopes, or provide a blocked -> arbitrating edge for the case where the collected evidence is intact and candidate-bound. Discarding sound evidence to recover from a clock is the most expensive possible answer.
