## 2026-08-22T22:58:08Z T009 ledger (operator e40)
--summary First real operator feedback on orchid judgment pages: cryptic, unclear what is being approved, and the reply is hard to act on --detail Ledger item, and the most direct evidence this task has. The operator received live judgment pages on telegram on 2026-08-22, after the notification chain was connected, and reported in their own words: the approval is difficult to copy and paste; it is hard to know what is being approved or unblocked or proceeded with; and the message is just cryptic.

That is a USER describing the shipped behaviour, not a reviewer describing code. Three distinct failures in one sentence.

ONE, THE ACTION IS UNCLEAR. The page says "judgment boundary [blocked-task] needs an operator" and names no task title, no round, and no statement of what the decision actually is. The operator cannot tell whether they are approving a candidate, clearing a block, waiving an attempt, or agreeing to something else entirely — and the boundary KINDS (blocked-task, review-conflict, operator-decision) are internal vocabulary that means nothing outside the codebase.

TWO, THE CHOICES ARE UNKNOWABLE. The reply template ends in the literal token <choice>, and libexec/orchid-answer accepts free text validated against nothing, so there is no set to enumerate and no way for the operator to learn what is acceptable. They guessed "proceed" and it was accepted, which is the worst outcome: an unvalidated free-text answer that looks like it worked.

THREE, THE REPLY IS PHYSICALLY AWKWARD. The message ends with a shell command carrying an absolute repository path, a qid and a sixteen-character nonce, to be copied and pasted accurately on a phone. Even when the operator knows what they want, acting on it is the hard part.

MITIGATION FOUND, NOT A FIX: the hermes gateway is an agent process with a tool registry, not a passive webhook, so a plain-language reply can plausibly be executed on the operator behalf without any copy-paste. That is worth documenting for operators, but it does not fix the page — an operator should not need an agent to interpret a notification that orchid itself composed.

THIS RAISES THE PRIORITY OF THE BODY-AND-CHOICES WORK ALREADY IN THIS TASK CRITERIA. The page must name the task and its title, the round, one line stating the decision in plain language, and the permitted answers. And a question must carry a declared choice set that orchid answer validates against, because until it does, no button, no plain-language reply, and no clearer wording can be trusted to mean what the operator intended.

## 2026-08-23T15:55:58Z T009 ledger (operator e43)
--summary A medium finding was dropped by re-review of an UNCHANGED candidate, and deterministic approval merged it --detail Ledger item, must-fix, and it is an integrity fault in the review record rather than a defect in any one candidate.

WHAT HAPPENED. Round a2 produced three envelopes against candidate 40ac15d2f9a2: two approve, and one request-changes carrying a MEDIUM — the judgment page prints the stored attempts field, which is a COMPLETED count, so a first attempt renders as attempt zero. The task then re-reviewed. Round a3 produced two envelopes, both approve with only lows, bound to THE SAME candidate 40ac15d2f9a2 — the tree never changed by a byte. The driver then applied deterministic approval on the stated grounds of unanimous scope-complete approval from 2 reviews, no finding at or above medium, and moved the task to merging. The medium was never addressed, never withdrawn, and never seen by an arbiter.

THE MECHANISM: deterministic approval counts only the CURRENT round envelopes. A finding filed against a candidate in an earlier round does not survive into the next round even when the candidate is byte-identical. So a medium can be erased simply by re-reviewing the same tree until a quieter pair of reviewers arrives. Nothing about that is deliberate — but nothing prevents it either, and it is indistinguishable from a defect being fixed.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THIS INSTANCE. The finding is small (an off-by-one in a message), but the shape is that review verdicts are not durable against their candidate. Two adjacent tasks in this run already exist for neighbouring problems: T032 (stop deterministic approval overriding an arbiter request-changes) and T039 (pin the review plan for an attempt so collected evidence keeps counting). Neither covers this case, which is findings rather than plans or arbiter verdicts.

WHAT TO FIX: a finding bound to a candidate_sha must remain in force for as long as that sha is the candidate, and deterministic approval must consider every unwithdrawn finding bound to the current candidate, not merely those filed in the current round. If a later round genuinely disproves an earlier finding, that should require a reviewer or arbiter to say so explicitly, not merely to be silent about it.

THE INSTANCE ITSELF: libexec/orchid-notify:162 reads attempts from frontmatter and prints it as the round number. It should print attempts + 1, pinned by a case asserting a first attempt reads as 1. Carried as a follow-up rather than blocking the merge, since the page is still a large improvement on the cryptic one the operator complained about and the error is cosmetic in a line that did not exist before.

## 2026-08-23T17:19:14Z run lesson (operator e44)
L043 added (repo): THE OPERATOR MISTAKES IN THIS RUN ARE PROCEDURAL, NOT JUDGEMENTAL, AND THEY REPEAT. Counted on 2026-08-23 after the user asked why the same errors keep happening. Hand-ran drive, merge or launch alongside a live supervisor FOUR times (one CAS collision that stalled a merge 70 minutes, one duplicate supervisor, one stray pid-0 manifest gc cannot reap). Wrote a zsh for-loop over an unquoted variable THREE times, each running zero iterations and reporting success. Broke shell quoting in a --reason THREE times (backticks executing as command substitution, an apostrophe closing the string, nested double quotes). Rebased without re-pinning once, blocking a task on a stale checksum. Hardcoded ORCHID_EPOCH for a whole session while redirecting stderr to /dev/null, so every refusal after the epoch advanced was invisible. Exported ORCHID_CONCURRENCY into a supervisor, where it descended into every test fixture and failed every candidate suite. Used mv to replace a file and stripped its exec bit. Wrote "nothing further is asked of you" into a field that persists into the next rework brief, causing an implementer to file an empty round. Read a PREVIOUS attempt review envelopes as if they were the current round. NONE OF THESE WAS A DECISION. Every one was a step skipped or a shell subtlety in an operation performed many times, which is the exact class a checklist removes and the exact class experience does not. Judgement improved over the run; procedure did not, because procedure was carried in memory. WHAT THIS ARGUES FOR: any operator procedure performed more than twice should be a SCRIPT THAT VERIFIES ITS OWN POSTCONDITIONS, not a remembered sequence. The first one written is scratchpad/op-rebase.sh, which refuses when a supervisor is live, refuses a dirty tree, refuses a status where a rebase would unbind review evidence, records file modes before and compares after, always re-pins with the hand-off trailer, and then CHECKS on-target, pin freshness and mode stability rather than assuming them. Its refusal message names the reason and the alternative. The same treatment belongs on arbitration (verify findings against source; confirm the envelopes are bound to the CURRENT candidate and attempt) and on brief-writing (supersede line first, numbered actions, the exact commands that must exit 0, never a sentence that could read as "no further work").

## 2026-08-25T18:29:08Z T038 note (operator e49)
--summary r-002 retrospective written at docs/r-002-retrospective.md; run frozen at 15 of 40 --detail Written by the operator on freezing the run rather than by an implementer, because the run is being accepted at 15 of 40 rather than completed and T038 was never dispatched.

WHAT IT RECORDS. The governance kernel worked and the operability layer did not, and that distinction is the result. On the working side: review caught genuine defects every time the operator verified one against source; merge revalidation caught the OPERATOR when an exported ORCHID_CONCURRENCY leaked into every test fixture; evidence binding held, so where evidence went missing it was lost rather than forged; and arbitration held a consistent standard across roughly forty judgments including against the operator own preference.

ON THE FAILING SIDE it documents the characteristic defect (L028, the unescapable state) with all six confirmed mechanisms, and notes that the fourth arrived inside a fix for the third. It records in full the five-link chain that froze the run for two days: an engine finished its review, wrote its verdict to the log and exited without its envelope reaching reviews (F35); the undrained envelope counted as an engine failure; three failures excluded the engine permanently because consecutive_failures only resets on a success that can never happen; the excluded engine made a review tier independence unprovable; that raised a boundary; and drive exits 16 AT a boundary, before its dispatch and merge sections, so forty-eight jobs sat prepared with pid 0 that jobs gc cannot reap (F41). One jobs reconcile recovered the envelope intact. The engine had never been broken.

IT ALSO STATES WHAT THE OPERATOR GOT WRONG, because a retrospective that only indicts the tool is not honest: procedure rather than judgement was the failure mode (L043) — four hand-runs alongside a live supervisor, three duplicate supervisors, four zsh word-splitting bugs, three quoting failures, a rebase without a re-pin, a session-long hardcoded epoch behind >/dev/null; under-fixing the boundary halt so the supervisor reported it 337 times across 330 frozen passes; reading the L020 label instead of re-deriving it, which hid five of its six sites; and above all the ordering error of L041.

RECOMMENDATION RECORDED: accept r-002 on what it proved rather than what it shipped, do not declare beta, and carry the remaining twenty-five tasks to r-003 with the bootstrap set scheduled FIRST, treating "a guard that refuses must name the action that clears it" as an invariant with a test enumerating every refusal path — one rule that covers six of this run defects.

--summary r-002 FROZEN at 15 of 40 by operator decision; 25 tasks carry to r-003 with the bootstrap set scheduled first --detail Ledger item. Run frozen 2026-08-25. Supervisor stopped, drive stopped, monitor stopped. Nothing is dispatching.

FROZEN STATE: integration 1b781c3 (merge T005), epoch 49, 15 of 40 merged, 43 lessons recorded. Task states: 17 rework, 15 done, 4 pending, 2 reviewing, 1 testing, 1 implementing. ZERO blocked, ZERO stale manifests, all four engines available. Of 36 task worktrees, 21 are on integration and 15 are behind. No work is lost: every carried task keeps its worktree and commits, and the fifteen conflicted branches from the 2026-08-20 unwind remain preserved as r002-preserve/<task> tags.

MERGED (15): T001 T002 T003 T004 T005 T006 T008 T010 T013 T014 T017 T020 T022 T028 T040.

CARRYING TO r-003 (25): T007 T009 T011 T012 T015 T016 T018 T019 T021 T023 T024 T025 T026 T027 T029 T030 T031 T032 T033 T034 T035 T036 T037 T038 T039.

RETROSPECTIVE at docs/r-002-retrospective.md. Its conclusion: the governance kernel worked and the operability layer did not, and that distinction is the result. Review caught real defects every time they were verified against source; merge revalidation caught the operator; evidence binding held. What failed was the run keeping itself running.

r-003 ORDERING IS RECORDED IN docs/plans/r-003-requirements.md AS TRACK 0, AS A GATE RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE: T026, T027, T019, T030, T039, T035 run to completion before anything else dispatches. This exists because of L041 — orchid dispatches in task-id order and cannot express priority, every task that repairs the run is numbered above T025, and r-002 therefore hit each defect while its own fix sat pending. Track 0 also carries the six defects r-002 found that no task owns: drive halting the whole run at one boundary (L026), envelopes never drained (F35), the engine ledger having no recovery path, findings not being durable against their candidate, boundaries not withdrawn when their condition clears, and dispatch worktrees never being removed.

RUN-LEVEL GATE PROPOSED FOR r-003: the L028 invariant — a guard that can refuse must name, at the point of refusal, the supported action that clears it, and if no verb provides that action the guard is not finished — shipped as a test enumerating every refusal path. One rule covering six of this run confirmed defects.

NOT CLAIMED: beta readiness, third-party qualification, or any release. Version remains 1.0.0-beta.x.
